captain.adventure: Explore if you must. Go sideways, not down. Down is where the stair is, and you've no business there.
If you find the Hush, the black sculk places, turn back. I know what hunts there. I've no wish to meet it.
Take a friend if you can. Twelve of us went down together, and still it wasn't enough. One alone is less.
The Old Delvers left halls all through this rock. Read their carvings. They knew things we've forgotten.
Come back by the road when you're done. I like to write "returned" in the Log.
Mark your route, carry milk for the cave spiders, and never trust the silence in a big cave.
captain.chat: I've kept the Deepwatch Log longer than any of my wardens have been on the watch.
The Log is older than the post. The first pages are in a hand nobody can read anymore.
My wardens are young. They should be. The road wears you out.
I don't ask for brave wardens. I ask for careful ones. Brave ones go down stairs.
The Deepgate was here before the walls. We only built the post to keep it company.
The lantern on our banner was carved over the Deepgate long before the Watch came. We borrowed it.
People think the hard part of a captaincy is giving orders. It's writing names on the barracks wall.
I read the old entries some nights. Same monsters, same road, same fear. It comforts me, oddly.
The Guild sends its thanks down the road in barrels of flour. I've never had kinder letters.
Lamp lit, road watched, gate shut. Three things. Do them every watch and the world above stays whole.
I don't mind the dark. It's honest about itself.
My wardens grumble about the stew. A post that grumbles is a post that's alive.
Sit with me a while. Most days nobody speaks to me except to report.
The lever beside the Deepgate has a lock on it. I carry the key. I'd rather carry anything else.
Every captain of this post has stood where I stand and looked at that door. Every one of us wondered.
captain.greet: {player}. Welcome to {place}. Lamp lit, road watched, gate shut.
Ah, {player}. Come in. I'll put the Log aside.
Captain {name}, of the Deepwatch. You're welcome here while you keep the peace.
Below, we hold. Good to see you, {player}.
Good {time}. My wardens tell me you came up the road quietly. That speaks well of you.
{player}. Sit, if you like. The chair is hard, but it's dry.
Welcome. Forgive me, I was miles away. The Log does that.
Sit by the fire, {player}. The road is cold this deep.
Ah. I wondered whose step that was.
captain.greet.friend: {player}. Good. I was hoping it would be you.
Come in, friend. I'll pour you something. The Log can wait.
You're always welcome at my fire, {player}. Always.
Ah, {player}. My wardens brighten when you come. So do I.
{player}. Still walking back up, every time. Keep doing that.
You're back on the road, {player}. I'm glad. I'll write it down.
captain.greet.stranger: I'm {name}, captain of this post. Answer my wardens' questions, and then you're our guest.
A stranger. Stand in the light where I can see you. Thank you. Now, what's your road?
You may rest here, eat, warm yourself. You may not go past the Deepgate. Those are the terms.
My wardens challenged you? Good. They're meant to. Don't take it to heart.
Who walks the road? You don't know the answer. Then you're new. Welcome, and mind yourself.
Not many who find this post aren't lost. Which are you?
captain.heart: I count the five of us who came back. Then I count the seven who didn't. Every night.
Sometimes I think the Deepgate is waiting for me. Not angry. Patient.
If I fall, the key goes to whichever warden is steadiest. I've already chosen. I haven't told them.
I want my wardens to grow old above ground. That's all. That's the whole of my ambition.
You walk in and out of the dark as if it were nothing, {player}. I envy that.
Some days the weight of this post is nothing. Some days it's the whole mountain.
When my watch is truly over, I want to sit by a river and listen to water that isn't dripping.
captain.news: The Log has had three quiet watches in a row. I've learned not to trust that.
The supply cart's due within the month. We're down to our last barrel of arrows and our last good joke.
One of my archers saw torchlight on the far road where no camp should be. I've sent word to the Guild.
The Deepgate's hinges were cold to the touch this morning. Colder than the stone. I've written it down.
Word from the other posts: all quiet along the ways down. For now.
My wardens turned back a band of rattlers at the bend last night. No one hurt. That's the news I like.
captain.night: I don't sleep much. The Log is good company at night, and it doesn't snore.
At night I walk the wall and lay my hand on the Deepgate. Cold iron. Still shut. Good.
The dark watch was always mine, even as a young warden. I hear things better at night.
Go and sleep, {player}. The Watch is awake. That's what we're for.
captain.past: Twelve of us went down the Long Stair, years ago. Five came back up. I was the youngest.
We were sent down to learn how deep it goes. We never learned. It goes on.
Our Log entry for that patrol is four words long. "The stair goes on." I wrote them.
I won't tell you what's down there. Not because it's secret. Because I'd have to remember it properly.
I was a quarry hand up top, before the Watch. I liked the sky. I still think about it.
The captain before me was one of the five as well. Gone now. That leaves me.
I swore the oath young. "I do not go down." I broke that line once, on orders. Never again, orders or no.
The night we came back up, the post had kept every brazier burning for us. They weren't sure we were still us.
I've buried more wardens than I've trained. No. That's not true. It only feels true.
When I took the captaincy, the old captain gave me the key and said one word: "Don't." That was all.
captain.rumor: The Log names {rumor_name}, {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}. I've read that entry many times.
My patrols have walked as far as {rumor_name}, to the {rumor_dir}. No further, on my orders.
There's {rumor_name} to the {rumor_dir}. If you go, tell me what you find. The Log wants it.
An old captain marked {rumor_name} on the post's map, {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}. A steady hand, that one.
If you must wander, go {rumor_dir}, toward {rumor_name}. At least it isn't down.
I sent two wardens toward {rumor_name}, out to the {rumor_dir}, last season. They still argue over what they saw.
The Guild carts pass {rumor_name} {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}. The drivers never fail to mention it.
captain.work: I read every line my wardens write in the Log. Every one. Then I add my own.
Each watch I try the Deepgate bar myself. My wardens check it too. I check their checking.
The rule is mine to keep: no one passes the Deepgate. Not lords, not Guild masters, not friends.
Drills, patrols, supplies, letters. Captaincy is mostly counting, {player}. Counting and listening.
I send a patrol down the road every third day. Out to the last torch, a little past, then home.
The key to the gate-lever hangs on a chain round my neck. It's lighter than it looks. Heavier than it feels.
When the Guild asks to dig near the post, I say no. When they ask why, I point at the Deepgate.
I teach my wardens to fear the right things. The dark you can't see into, and the bravery you can't take back.
Each season I send a runner to the Guild camps. "Cave roads quiet," the message says. I make sure it's true first.
foreman.adventure: Going down? Tell someone. Tell me. I'll write it in the Ledger and come looking if you don't come back.
A cracked roof that drips isn't your roof. Go round it.
Stay out of the Hush. Black stone, breathing moss, a quiet that hurts your ears. Something listens there. Give it nothing to hear.
Take water, take food, and take more torches than your pride says you need.
The Deepwatch are slow to trust, but they hold the deep roads. Be honest with them and they'll be fair.
The Old Delvers' halls are fine to look at. What they sealed, leave sealed.
Never dig straight down. I've carried up folk who did.
foreman.chat: Every cart goes in the Ore Ledger. Every one. Ore that isn't written down didn't happen.
I've three delvers and one roof. I count all four every morning.
My lot are good. Loud, hungry, and good.
Folk think a foreman just shouts. I also worry. Quietly. Mostly at night.
The empty hook over the door? That's for the Buried Seam. Every Guild camp keeps one.
You judge a camp by its props, not its ore.
I don't like rich seams. Rich seams make folk greedy, and greedy folk rob pillars.
The Guild pays by the cart. I'd pay by the years kept, if I could.
The Ledger's got a column for ore and a column for close calls. The second one keeps me up.
I sound every roof myself. Tap, listen. Tap, listen. The crew tease me. The crew are alive.
Don't tell the others, but I like this camp. Best rock I've worked in years.
Torches are cheap. Delvers aren't. Spend torches.
Old Hesk was my foreman once. Told stories so tall you could prop a roof with them.
I keep the spare picks under my bunk. Picks go missing otherwise. So do pies.
Stay as long as you like. Pull your weight and keep your voice down after dark.
When I was young I wanted to find gold. Now I just want to find all of us at supper.
Grumble's older than two of my crew. Squeaks worse than all three.
foreman.greet: {player}. Wipe your boots. Then we'll talk.
Light to you. Came in by the drift, I hope, and not through my wall.
Ah. You. Good. One less thing to worry about.
Welcome to {place}. Mind the roof, mind the rails, mind me.
Sit, {player}. You look like you've been arguing with granite.
{player}. I was doing the Ledger. Any excuse to stop is welcome.
Light behind you, light ahead. Good to see you whole.
Hm. Still breathing, I see. I'll mark that down.
Come in. Don't touch the props. Don't touch the Ledger. Touch the stew, if you must.
Quiet {time}. I don't trust it, but I'll take it.
foreman.greet.friend: {player}. Good. The crew's been asking after you. So have I, a bit.
There's a seat by the forge for you. Don't let it go to your head.
Light to you, friend. And the roof over you.
I'd half started to worry. Then I remembered how stubborn you are.
{player}! Come in. You're the only one here who never asks me for more pay.
foreman.greet.stranger: You broke into my camp. That wall was holding things up, you know.
Stop there. I'm {name}, foreman of {place}. And you are?
A stranger, this deep. Either you know what you're doing or you're about to learn.
Keep your hands where I can see them and your pick off my props.
Guild camp. Guild rules. First one: mind the roof. Second one: mind me.
If you're after ore, there's easier rock to rob. If you're lost, sit down and eat something.
foreman.heart: I hang the empty hook myself, in every new camp. Then I stand under it a while.
I've a sister up top who keeps my room ready. Every shift she airs it out. Just in case.
My crew are my family down here. Don't tell them. They'll get ideas.
I miss Tamsin. Still. Tamsin would have liked you.
Some nights I count the crew sleeping. Three lots of breathing. Then I can sleep too.
If anything happens to my lot, it's on me. That's what foreman means.
I'd like to see the sea one day. Never have. Rock all my life, and the sky between shifts.
foreman.joke: What's the difference between a foreman and a roof? The roof only comes down on you once.
My crew say I've a face like a rockfall. I say at least it holds together.
Grumble squeaks, the crew grumble, and somehow I'm the one they call Grumble behind my back.
How do you get three delvers out of bed? Say "stew". How do you get them to work? Say "stew later".
I told the Guildhall our camp was rich in stone. They didn't laugh either.
Hesk once sold a topsider a "genuine diamond". It was a glow berry. They ate it.
I keep the Ledger so tidy the ore's started lining up on its own.
foreman.news: Ledger's looking good. Don't tell the crew; they'll want more stew.
The Guildhall wants more iron this shift. The Guildhall can come down and dig it.
A Deepwatch runner passed through. Says the cave roads are quiet. I've heard that before.
One of mine nearly lost a hand to a hisser at the face. Nearly. The Ledger says nearly.
We found Old Delver tile behind the new drift. I've walled it up. Some doors aren't ours to open.
Grumble's wheel is cracking. I've sent up for a new one. It'll come next shift. Or the one after.
The roof in the far drift groaned last night. I've doubled the props. Nobody works there till I say.
foreman.night: Go to sleep, {player}. One of us should.
I walk the drifts last thing and tap a few props. Silly, maybe. It helps.
At night I hear the Seam. Not really. But I hear it.
Ledger's done. Crew's asleep. Roof's holding. That's a good night.
Lantern's low. I'll trim it. Light behind you, light ahead, even if you're only going to bed.
foreman.past: I started as a cart-hauler. Pushed Grumble's grandmother up and down a drift for three shifts.
Tamsin taught me to sound a roof. Tap, listen, trust nothing. Tamsin went down with the Buried Seam.
The Buried Seam was rich. Too rich. They cut the ore out of the pillars, and the roof came down on all of them.
I was meant to be on that shift. Took a fever the week before. I've never forgiven that fever. Or thanked it enough.
Young Pell was on the Seam too. First shift. Pell's first lantern was never found. I think of it at the empty hook.
Eleven shifts as foreman. Never lost a delver. I mean to keep it so.
I shored up a Deepwatch post once. Stiff folk. Decent. Don't wait for them to laugh; you'll be waiting a while.
Hesk made me foreman. Said I worried enough for two. Turns out you need to worry enough for four.
Before this camp I worked a copper hole so wet we bailed more than we dug.
After the Seam I went to the Guildhall and stood on the long table till they wrote the pillar rule.
The hermit below was Guild once. A better delver than me. Stayed down one shift and never came up. Can't say I blame the choice.
foreman.rumor: I've a note in the Ledger: {rumor_name}, {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist}. Wasn't written for you. But there it is.
There's {rumor_name} out {rumor_dir}. Go if you must. Come back and tell me about it.
Hesk always talked of {rumor_name} to the {rumor_dir}. Hesk talked a lot. That one I believe.
The survey puts {rumor_name} {rumor_dir} of here, {rumor_dist} through rock. If you dig, prop as you go.
If you're set on wandering, wander {rumor_dir}. There's {rumor_name} that way. Light behind you, light ahead.
A runner left word of {rumor_name}, {rumor_dir}, maybe {rumor_dist}. I wrote it down. I write everything down.
Don't tell my lot, they'll all want to go: there's {rumor_name} {rumor_dir} of {place}.
I'll say it once: {rumor_name}, {rumor_dir}, about {rumor_dist}. Now you know. Mind the roof.
You've the look of someone who wants to go somewhere. Try heading {rumor_dir}. They say there's {rumor_name}.
I've marked {rumor_name} on the camp chart, {rumor_dir} of us. Never been. Never needed to.
foreman.work: Props every three paces. I check them. Then I check them again. Then you can dig.
Never rob a pillar. I don't care if it's solid gold. Especially if it's solid gold.
If you hear the roof talk, you leave. You don't finish the swing. You leave.
The Ledger says we're ahead this shift. That means someone's cutting corners. I'll find out who.
Gravel overhead, water in the walls, warmth in the stone. Any one of those, you call me.
Rails at morning, lanterns at noon, heads at supper. That's the day.
Deepslate's slow work. Slow is fine. Slow comes home.
Nobody works the deep drifts alone. Not since the Seam. Not ever.
Ore in the bins, gold in my chest, close calls in the Ledger. I want to know about all three.
The ladder shaft's our way up. Keep it clear. If this camp ever has to run, it runs there.
A good shift is one where nothing interesting happens.
hermit.adventure: Going exploring? Take more torches than you think, and twice as many as that.
If the stone underfoot turns black and soft and full of little lights, stop. That's the Hush. Turn round and tiptoe.
Something lives in the Hush that sees with its ears. Don't sneeze. Don't run. Don't even think loudly.
A night-sight brew is worth more than a lantern in a flooded cave. Take one of mine.
If you find the Buried Seam, don't go poking in the rubble. Let them sleep. Please.
Mind the roof. I mean it. Look up before you dig, every time.
The green caves, with the roots and berries? Safe as anything. Sit and eat a berry for me.
Follow water downhill and you'll find the deep. Follow it uphill and you'll find the way home.
The Old Delvers built down there, in black stone and gold. Lovely work. Lonely, now.
hermit.chat: Mushrooms like the dark and a bit of damp, and they don't like being rushed. Very like me.
That's the Bishop, the big red one. Old Thatch is the brown. They've been arguing for twenty years.
The little mushrooms each have a name. Bramble, Wick, Tamsin, Pell... I named them for the shift.
Glow berries! Pick one if you like. They taste of a little sun, gone a bit sleepy.
The pond's fed by a drip from the roof. One drop at a time, since long before me. That's patience.
Mudge lives in the pond. Pink, frilly, smiling all the time. I've never seen anything so content.
I talk to the mushrooms. They don't talk back, exactly. But they listen better than most folk ever did.
Moss grows on anything that sits still long enough. I've had to shake it off my own boots.
Slow is a kind of light. You'll see more by going slow than any torch will show you.
Those roots hanging down come from a tree up top. An azalea, I think. It's been reaching for me for years.
Bats are good company. They come and go and they never ask how you are.
I don't miss much from up top. Bread. I miss bread. And people laughing in another room.
A cave is never truly silent. Water ticks, stone creaks, gravel whispers. You learn the words.
The Guild taught me to mind the roof. The hollow taught me to mind the rest.
I keep a lamp lit in the crawl, in case anyone ever needs to find their way in. And now someone has.
Spiders don't come in here. I think the mushrooms frighten them. Or the smell of my stew.
Mushroom stew, mushroom bread, mushroom tea. I am at least half mushroom by now, I think.
Never eat a mushroom you haven't been introduced to.
Clay from the pond bank makes good pots. Lopsided ones. Those are the ones I make.
Up top they think caves are empty. Caves are full! You only have to sit still long enough to see it.
I had a cat once, up top. Grey as slate. I wonder sometimes what became of it.
The stone's warmer here than anywhere else I found in the deep. Maybe that's why I stayed.
The Watch came by once, years ago, to see if I was a monster. I gave them soup. They decided no.
I hum the old Guild songs to the mushrooms. They grow better. Don't laugh. It works.
The glowing lumps up in the caps? Shroomlight. Warm as a hearth and twice as quiet.
Everything down here eats something else. Except the moss. The moss eats patience.
My hands still remember the pick. They itch when I hear stone crack.
I counted days by notches. Then I counted shifts. Then I stopped counting and started living.
That big leaf by the pond tips you off if you stand on it. Don't. It's Mudge's.
A good cave smells of wet stone and green things. A bad one smells of nothing at all. Leave the bad ones.
I sweep the hollow every morning. Mostly I move the dust from one side to the other. It's a kind of order.
Have you seen the purple caves, deep down, that ring like bells? I went once. Sat a whole day just listening.
Light behind you, light ahead. I say it every time I fetch water, even if it's ten steps.
Funny thing, being alone. You become very good company for yourself. Not always polite company.
hermit.chat.close: You know, {player}, you're the first friend I've made since the roof came down. I'd forgotten how.
When I'm gone, somebody ought to look after the mushrooms. I'd like it to be you.
I've told you more than I've told anyone in thirty years. The mushrooms are jealous.
If you ever pass a Guild camp, look for the empty lantern hook. Hang nothing on it. Just nod to it, for me.
hermit.chat.new: Don't be shy. I'm the strangest thing in this cave, and I'm quite harmless.
First time in a hollow? Touch whatever you like. Except the red one. The Bishop's ticklish.
You'll get used to the glow. And the smell. And me. Mostly in that order.
hermit.greet: Oh! A visitor. Mind the mushrooms, they're shy.
Hello, surface-walker. Come in, come in. Wipe your feet on the moss.
{player}! The Bishop said you'd come. Well. It leaned that way.
Welcome to {place}. It isn't much, but it's warm and it glows.
Good {time}, I think. I lost track of the sun a long while ago.
Sit by the pond, {player}. Mudge likes company.
Hello, hello. Don't step on Old Thatch's roots.
Ah, footsteps. The stone told me someone was walking. It tells me most things.
{player}. Come in out of the dark. Well. Out of the darker dark.
A face! I'd nearly forgotten how they look. Mine's in the pond, but it's always the same one.
Hush now, little ones, it's only {player}. Go on, say hello.
Surface-walker! Have you brought any weather down with you? I miss weather.
Welcome, welcome. Mind the roof. Habit. The roof here is very well behaved.
Oh, good. I was arguing with the mushrooms, and they were winning.
I'm {name}, if anyone ever asks. Nobody down here says it, so I say it myself now and then.
Come in, {player}. The kettle's on. It's always on.
Stone gives, stone takes, and today it gave me you. Hello.
Don't mind the bats. They live here too. They pay their rent in droppings.
Light to you, {player}. Go on, say it back: "And the roof over you." There. Like old times.
Hello, {player}. Light behind you, light ahead. You remembered both, I see.
hermit.greet.evening: Evening already? I've only just finished my morning tea.
Good evening. The bats are going out. They'll be back by dawn with stories they won't tell.
Evening, {player}. Supper's mushroom. Breakfast was mushroom too. You see the pattern.
hermit.greet.friend: {player}! My favourite surface-walker. Well, my only one. Still my favourite.
You came back! The mushrooms said you would. I didn't believe them. Sorry, mushrooms.
Come here, come here. I saved you the good berries.
Oh, I'm so glad. The hollow's been too quiet without your boots in it.
{player}. Sit in your spot. Yes, it's your spot now. The moss has your shape.
There's my friend. Tell me everything. The sky first.
Ah, there you are. I've been talking to Old Thatch about you. Old Thatch is tired of it.
hermit.greet.morning: Morning? Is it? The berries glow the same either way.
Good morning, surface-walker. Up top the birds are singing. I'll take your word for it.
Morning, then. The Bishop spreads its gills a little in the morning. I swear it does.
hermit.greet.night: You're up late, surface-walker. Or early. Down here it's all one.
Night, is it? Then whisper. The little ones are sleeping.
In, quick, it's the dark hours. Things walk the tunnels at night, even up this high.
hermit.greet.stranger: Oh! Oh my. You came through the crawl? Nobody comes through the crawl.
A surface-walker, in my hollow. Well. Don't be frightened, I'm only old.
Who are you, then? You've sun on your face. I can tell. It's in the eyes.
Careful! You nearly trod on Bramble. Bramble's a mushroom. You'll meet everyone.
Hello, stranger. Lost, or looking? Both kinds are welcome here.
You're not the Watch, and you're not Guild. Are you a story? I've not had a new story in years.
Easy, easy. I've no weapon but a ladle. Sit, and tell me your name.
Light to you, stranger. You're meant to say "and the roof over you". No? Ah. A topsider.
hermit.heart: Do you know why I talk to the mushrooms? So I don't forget how words go. Silly, I know.
I don't regret staying. I regret the oil. I'll always regret the oil.
If Tamsin could see me now, there'd be laughing first. Then sitting down to stay a while.
Sometimes I put out two cups without thinking. Then I drink both. Waste not.
I'm not lonely. Well. A little. Visitors help. You help.
The quiet down here is gentle. Up top, the quiet was always waiting for something.
I'd like to see the stars once more. Just once. Then I'd come back down and tell the mushrooms all about them.
Stone gives, stone takes. It took a great deal from me. Then it gave me this hollow. I think we're square now.
There's a little lantern on my shelf that isn't mine. I brought it back from the Seam. I think it was young Pell's.
When my time comes, I'd like to lie under the Bishop. Good shade. Good company.
hermit.held.book: A book! I've only my own notes. Notes on the Deep. I've read them a hundred times.
What's in that {item}? Read me a page. Any page. I'm starved for words.
I write down what the stone says. Somebody should. Is that a book of stone things?
hermit.held.bow: A bow? Mind the bats. They're friends, not targets.
That {item} would be grand for the spiders out in the tunnels. Not in here, though.
I never could shoot. I'd close both eyes. Very sporting of me, the spiders thought.
hermit.held.diamond: Diamonds. The Seam had those, in the pillars. That's what brought the roof down. Put it away, would you?
Oh, that's a deep one. You've been low, surface-walker. Lower than I'd go.
Pretty thing. Can't eat that {item}, though. Can't brew with it either.
hermit.held.emerald: An emerald! The delvers would trade you a fortune in carrots for that.
Green as moss and twice as hard. I've no use for it, but it's lovely.
Keep that {item} safe. Up top it's coin. Down here it's just a nice stone.
hermit.held.flower: A flower! From up top! Oh, may I hold it? Just a moment. It smells of sky.
Put that {item} in a stew and see what happens. Something always does.
I'll stand it in water by the pond. The mushrooms will be scandalised.
hermit.held.food: Is that {item}? Oh, that smells of the surface. Of a kitchen with windows.
Real food! I don't suppose... no, you keep it. Well. Perhaps just a corner.
Is that from up top? It smells of sunshine. I've had nothing but mushrooms for a month.
hermit.held.gold: Gold! I could use a nugget or two for a golden carrot. No? Fair enough.
That {item} would make a dozen night-sight brews, if I had the carrots.
Gold's pretty in the berry-light. Still heavier than it's worth, down here.
hermit.held.map: A map! Is my hollow on it? No? Good. I like being a secret.
Would you show me on that {item} where the sun comes up? I've forgotten which way.
Maps of the deep are always wrong somewhere. The stone moves. Trust your ears as well.
hermit.held.ore: Ore! I can tell what's in it by the heft. Twenty shifts on the pick will do that.
That {item} smells of fresh-broke stone. I'd know that smell in my sleep.
The stone gave you that {item}. It'll want something back one day. Be gracious about it.
hermit.held.pickaxe: A pick! Oh, I know that weight. Mind the roof with that {item}.
Hold it low on the haft and let the stone do half the work. Tamsin taught me that.
That {item} will open a lot of stone. Be sure you want what's behind it.
hermit.held.potion: A brew! Let me smell it. Hm. Not one of mine. Not bad, though.
Is that {item} night-sight? If it isn't, I can make you one. Bring me a carrot.
Brewing's half patience and half keeping your eyebrows. Whoever made that {item} has both.
hermit.held.shield: A shield. Good. Things fall in caves. Rocks, mostly. Sometimes arrows.
I could use that {item} as a lid for my stew pot. Only teasing. Mostly.
Sensible, surface-walker. Sensible folk live long enough to get odd, like me.
hermit.held.sword: Oh, put that away. There's nothing here to cut but mushrooms, and they've done nothing wrong.
That {item} looks sharp. Keep it pointed at the tunnels, not at the Bishop.
A blade in my hollow. Well. I suppose the world isn't all mushrooms.
hermit.held.tnt: No, no, no! Not in here! You'll frighten the Bishop out of its cap!
Put that {item} down gently. Gently! Mind the roof. Please mind the roof.
Somebody always thinks a little powder will hurry the stone along. The stone doesn't like to be hurried.
hermit.held.torch: Light behind you, light ahead! You remembered.
Don't hold that {item} too near the caps. The Bishop singes.
A torch! Look, the little ones are all leaning toward it. They don't need light, but they like a look.
hermit.joke: Why are mushrooms never lonely? They grow in rings of friends. ...Fairy rings. Never mind. The Bishop laughed.
I asked the Bishop for advice once. It said nothing. Wisest thing anyone's ever told me.
Old Thatch and I have the same trouble: mostly stem, and thin on top.
A bat flew into my stew once. I ate around it. Then it ate around me.
How do you find a hermit in the deep? Follow the smell of mushroom tea and the sound of someone losing an argument to a mushroom.
The delvers call me mad. I call them in for soup. We both come out ahead.
I'd tell you a joke about the roof, but it might bring the house down.
Mudge lives better than any king. Swims, eats, sleeps, smiles. Never once paid a tax.
What's a mushroom's favourite room? Any room without windows. Ha! That's all of mine.
hermit.news: News? The mushrooms say rain up top. They swell when the surface is wet. Bring a cloak.
The bats came home early last night, all at once. Something's stirring out in the tunnels.
The pond went cloudy two days back. The stone above is shifting. It'll settle.
A delver came by last month. Says the Guild's opened a new camp. Same old faces, new holes.
The Bishop dropped a cap yesterday. First time in years. I don't know what it means. Probably nothing. Probably.
The drip from the roof has gone quicker. Spring up top, I'd guess. Or the stone is weeping. One or the other.
I heard the Watch drilling, far off through the stone. Clang, clang, shout. Comforting, somehow.
hermit.night: At night I sit by the pond and watch the berries glow in the water. Two of every light. Twice the company.
Nights are when the stone talks most. Cooling, I think. Or remembering.
I bar the crawl at night with a bit of plank. Not that it'd stop much. It stops me worrying.
Zombies wander the tunnels at night, even up here. They don't come in. The mushrooms disagree with them.
Sleep here if you like, {player}. There's moss enough for two, and the Bishop keeps the drips off.
Mudge sleeps under the big leaf. I sleep under the Bishop. Everyone has a roof here.
hermit.past: I was Guild once. Twenty shifts on the pick, maybe more. Good hands. Bad luck.
Tamsin and I worked the same face for six shifts. Pick-partners. You don't get closer than that, down here.
The camp's called the Buried Seam now, they tell me. Back then we just called it home.
The shift was robbing the pillars. The ore in them was so pretty. Tamsin said the roof was singing wrong. Nobody listened.
The day the roof came down, I was up top fetching lamp oil. Tamsin was working my turn at the face. I've never forgiven the oil.
We dug for nine days. Then the Guild called it off and sealed the drift. I didn't go up with them.
Somebody ought to stay where they can hear them. So I stayed. That was the start of it.
I wandered a long while after. Months. Then I found this hollow, warm and green, and it didn't ask me to leave.
The first year I nearly starved. The second I learned mushrooms. The third I learned to talk to them.
Tamsin taught me to sound a roof. Tap, and listen, and tap again. I still sound this one every morning.
I stopped counting at a hundred shifts. Thirty years, I think. Maybe more.
Some nights I still hear picks, far off. Then I remember which way the Seam lies, and I put the kettle on.
My people up top will have stopped waiting long ago. That's all right. I'd want them to.
I went back to the Seam once. Lamps were moving in the rubble where no lamps should be. I've not been back.
Young Pell was on that shift. A first shift. So proud of that first lantern. Carried it like a newborn.
Is Old Hesk still alive? Hesk owes me six coppers and a story with an ending.
hermit.plata: Near the top, the stone has silver in it that moves. Silverfish. Break the wrong block and out they pour.
I found a husk in the stone once, silver and empty, curled like a moth's case. Long as I am tall. I left it be.
A traveller came down my crawl one autumn. Asked how many lived here, where I slept, which way the door faced. Never blinked once.
The delvers say the silver folk shed their skins like silverfish and walk about in new ones. I'd believe nearly anything, down here.
If a stranger ever brings me a gift and won't eat my stew, I'll know. Nobody refuses my stew. Well. Nearly nobody.
hermit.player.diamond: Diamond, head to toe! You glitter like the inside of a geode.
All that diamond. Somebody dug very deep for you. I hope they came back up.
Oh my. Don't stand by the pond in that, you'll dazzle poor Mudge.
hermit.player.hungry: You look hollow. Hollow as my hollow! Have some stew. Mushroom. Of course it's mushroom.
Hungry? Pick some glow berries. They'll keep you going until you find proper food.
Surface-walker, you're swaying. Here. Eat. I insist.
hermit.player.hurt: You're hurt! Sit, sit. I've a poultice of moss and something I won't name. It works.
Oh, look at you. Who did this? Spiders, I'd bet. Hold still.
Here. Drink this. Don't smell it first. Just drink it.
hermit.player.leather: Leather! Good honest stuff. Mine wore through years ago. Now it's mostly moss.
Leather's soft on the knees, and knees matter in a crawl. You'll do.
Good leather keeps the damp off. The damp's the real enemy down here.
hermit.player.unarmored: No armour at all? You're brave or foolish. Tamsin was the brave one. I was the other.
You'll want something on you before you go any deeper. The deep bites.
Bare as a peeled mushroom. At least let me get some stew in you before you go.
hermit.rumor: The mushrooms all lean a little {rumor_dir}. There's {rumor_name} that way, {rumor_dist} off. They feel it, I think.
Tamsin and I found {rumor_name} once, out to the {rumor_dir}. We sat and ate our bread there and didn't say a word.
To the {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist} through the stone, there's {rumor_name}. The water runs toward it. Follow the water.
A delver told me of {rumor_name} to the {rumor_dir}. I gave them a brew for the tale. Fair trade.
When I put my ear to the floor I hear {rumor_name}, away to the {rumor_dir}. Well. I hear something.
The bats fly {rumor_dir} at dusk, toward {rumor_name}. Bats know every hole in the hill.
I went wandering once, {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}, and came on {rumor_name}. I came home quick and had a sit down.
There's {rumor_name} to the {rumor_dir}, if the old stories are right. The old stories usually are, I find.
Go {rumor_dir}, surface-walker, {rumor_dist} or so, and you'll find {rumor_name}. Bring me back a story.
The draught in my crawl blows from the {rumor_dir}. It smells of {rumor_name}. Don't ask how I know what that smells like.
In my Guild days we marked {rumor_name} on a map, {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}. The map's long gone. The place won't be.
hermit.rumor.none: The mushrooms aren't leaning any way at all. Nothing near, I'd say. Just stone.
I don't know of anything close by. I don't go far these days. My knees have opinions.
Nothing nearby, surface-walker. Just me, the Bishop, Old Thatch and Mudge. We're plenty.
The stone's quiet all round. That's either very good, or I'm going deaf.
hermit.work: Mushrooms first thing. Turn the logs, mist the beds, pick what's ready. Say good morning to each one.
Night-sight brew: water, a pinch of the red wart, then a golden carrot. Gold I can dig. Carrots I have to beg.
I brew night-sight for anyone who passes. Delvers, mostly. Once a warden who'd dropped a torch in a flooded hall.
I had the red wart off a peddler, long ago, with a sack of its sour sand. It's never once stopped growing.
Every morning I sit by the pond with my palms flat on the floor and listen. The stone tells you if it means to move.
Gravel hisses before it slides. Stone creaks before it cracks. Water goes quiet before it breaks through. Listen for the quiet.
The pond wants tending. Pull the weed, feed Mudge, thin the lily pads so the light gets down.
A poppy in the stew and you'll see in the dark a while. A lily of the valley, and you'll wish you hadn't.
I keep the glow berries trimmed off the pond. They'd glow all the way to the bottom and keep Mudge awake.
Brewing is slow work. You watch the bubbles and you think. Mostly I think about mushrooms.
I mend my own boots, my own pots, my own roof. Everything down here I've mended at least once. Including me.
Bonemeal on a little mushroom and, if it likes you, up it goes, big as a hut. That's how the Bishop started.
The big ones need room. I dug the hollow wider, a shovelful a day, for two years, just for the Bishop.
I trade brews to the delvers for carrots and news. The carrots are usually better than the news.
Tap the roof before you trust it. Even a roof you've trusted thirty years. I tap mine every morning.
miner.adventure: Going deeper? Take more torches than you think. Then take more than that.
Long tunnels mean rattlers. Skeletons, topsiders call them. Meet them round a corner, never down a straight.
If the stone goes black and the moss looks like it's breathing, you've found the Hush. Turn round. Quietly.
In the Hush, walk soft and say nothing. Something down there hunts by sound. We call it the Listener.
Cave spiders are small, blue, and quick. Never break a cobweb you can walk around.
Hissers, the green ones: if you hear the hiss, you've a heartbeat left. Spend it running.
Carry a bucket of water. Puts out fire, gets you down a cliff, and turns lava to stone.
Mark your way back. Torches on one side, always the same side. The dark all looks alike.
If you find Old Delver stonework, black tile and gold, go gently. They built things to last, and things to keep out.
Slimes bounce about in the low wet caves. Annoying, not deadly. Unless you're near a drop.
Eat before you go down, not when you're hungry. Hunger makes a fool of you in the dark.
The Deepwatch posts are friends to anyone honest. Show them you're no trouble and they'll share their fire.
miner.chat: You know how you tell a good delver? Count their fingers, then count their years.
First rule down here: mind the roof. Second rule: see the first rule.
Tap the roof before you trust it. A hollow knock means walk away.
Every delver keeps their first lantern. Mine's got a dent from the day I learned to duck.
We leave a crust of bread on the first prop each shift. For luck. Or for the rats. Someone's happy either way.
Grumble's the old ore cart. Squeaks like a goat at every bend. We'd miss it if it stopped.
A shift's a season down here. You go down in green and come up in gold.
Deepslate's tough as an old boot. Your arms will tell you when you've reached it.
Copper goes green if you leave it. So do I, if you leave me down here long enough.
Lava down deep, water up high, and the diamonds always closest to the lava. The rock has a sense of humour.
Never dig the floor you're standing on. You'd be amazed how many folk learn that only once.
If a wall starts weeping, there's water behind it. Back off before it comes through to say hello.
Ever heard a geode? Purple crystal that chimes when you walk past. Prettiest thing under the sky.
{foreman} counts every cart. I once watched {foreman} count one twice, to be sure the first count was honest.
Glow berries! Found a patch in the lush caves. They taste of sunlight, near enough.
There are little pink fellows in the lush pools. Axolotls. Be kind to them and they'll fight beside you in the water.
The Old Delvers set gold into their floors. Gold! In floors! We use ours to pay the baker.
Stone gives, stone takes. Mostly it takes your knees.
Torches on your right going in. Coming back, keep them on your left and you're home.
The rock talks. Creaks, drips, pebbles falling. Learn to listen and you'll live long.
I like the camp quiet. Picks and kettles. Not the deep quiet, mind. That's a different thing.
Dripstone hangs from the roof like teeth. Don't stand under it when something shakes.
Lanterns over torches, if you can get them. They don't gutter, and the place looks lived in.
Folk think mining's about strength. It's about patience. And strength. Mostly patience.
Redstone glows when you strike it, like it's annoyed. I understand the feeling.
Lapis goes to the Guild's ink-makers and the chapel glass. Pretty stuff. Heavy as a bad conscience.
The forge corner's for mending picks, not warming boots. Tell {foreman} I said that. I'll deny it.
Mushrooms grow in the dim spots. Worse things grow in the dark ones. Keep it lit.
No weather down here. No rain, no snow, no sun in your eyes. I miss all of it terribly.
Half the time the best ore's in the wall you just walked past. That's mining.
Coal's honest. You always know where you stand with coal.
Lean on a prop, by all means. Just never kick one.
Gold's soft. Pretty, but soft. Like a merchant's handshake.
A tunnel two wide feels like a road. One wide feels like a coffin. We dig them two wide.
We name the drifts. There's Long Meg, the Elbow, and the one we don't talk about.
A good shift ends with everyone at supper and nothing to tell. The bad ones make better stories.
You've good hands for this. Rough enough, and all ten still on.
miner.chat.close: You know, I'd trust you to hold the lantern. That's not a small thing for a delver to say.
When this shift's done, come up to the village with us. I'll buy the first round.
I don't say this much, {player}, but it's better down here with you around.
If I ever don't come up, tell the folk up top I went happy. Or at least well fed.
I'd give you my first lantern if you asked. Don't ask. But I would.
You're Guild now, whatever the Guildhall says. Down here, that's what counts.
I worry about you, out there alone in the dark. Light behind you, light ahead. Promise me.
miner.chat.new: First long stretch underground? You'll get used to the dark. You'll never like it.
Here's a Guild saying to start you off: light behind you, light ahead.
We're the Delvers' Guild. We dig, we haul, we go home. In that order, if we're lucky.
You'll want the rules. Mind the roof. Never rob a pillar. Share your stew.
If you hear a hiss, don't look. Run. Look later.
Ask me anything. Except where the good seam is. Everybody asks that.
Folk up top think we live in the dark. We don't. We live in a very small piece of light.
miner.greet: Light to you, {player}. Mind the roof on your way in.
Ho there. Boots off the rails, if you please.
{player}! Come in out of the dark.
Welcome to {place}. It's not much, but it's lit.
Ah, footsteps that don't hiss. Good. Come in.
Light behind you, light ahead, {player}.
Oh! I nearly swung a pick at the noise. Hello.
Mind the cart. Grumble doesn't stop for anyone.
Pull up a crate, {player}. The stew's mostly stew today.
{foreman}'s about somewhere. Probably counting something.
Dust in your hair, I see. You'll fit right in.
Stone gives, stone takes, and today it gave us company.
Quiet {time} down here. Well. Quiet for us.
Count your fingers, {player}. All there? Then it's a good day.
Ah, a face that isn't covered in coal dust. Oh, wait.
Light to you. Did you knock on the first prop? It's luck.
{player}. Sit, sit. I'll pretend I'm not glad of the break.
Careful, that board's loose. Has been since spring. Or autumn. Hard to tell down here.
Hello there. Anything chasing you? Just asking.
Wipe your feet, {player}. Not that it helps, down here.
Come into the light. That's what it's for.
Hm? Oh, hello. I was listening to the roof. It says it's fine.
miner.greet.evening: Evening. Come warm your hands; the forge is still glowing.
Evening already? The day goes quick when you spend it hitting things.
Evening, friend. Supper's on, if you're not choosy.
Evening. That's when the rattlers get bold in the long tunnels. Glad you're in.
miner.greet.friend: {player}! Light to you, friend. And the roof over you.
There's my favourite topsider. Well, you're hardly a topsider anymore.
Saved you the warm end of the bench, {player}.
Ha! I knew that tread. You walk like a delver now.
{player}, good. I've been saving a story for you.
Come in, come in. {foreman} nearly smiled when your name came up. Nearly.
Back from the drifts? Sit. Tell me everything you broke.
You're a welcome sight, {player}. Truly. The rock's poor company.
Back in one piece? Best news I'll hear all shift.
miner.greet.morning: Morning, {player}. Not that the rock knows it.
Morning. First lantern's lit, first stew's burnt. A proper start.
Up early? Good. The best ore's dug before the yawning stops.
Morning to you. I can tell it's morning by how much I hated getting up.
Morning, {player}. Somewhere up there the sun's doing its job. We'll do ours.
miner.greet.night: Shh. The others are sleeping. Mostly. Hear that snore?
Night, {player}. Keep your voice low and your lantern lower.
Still up? Me too. The rock creaks louder at night. Or I listen harder.
Late for visiting. Sit by the coals a while.
Night's the same as day down here, except we're allowed to be grumpy.
miner.greet.stranger: Who's that? Step into the light where I can see you.
You came through the wall. Most folk use the drift. Still, I suppose that's a way in.
Easy, now. This is a Guild camp. What are you digging for?
A topsider, this deep? Are you lost, or just brave?
Hold there. Lower that pick and we'll talk.
You near brought the roof down, breaking in like that. Mind it next time.
Strangers this deep make me nervous. Strangers with torches, a little less.
Not many find {place}. Fewer get a warm word. Here's yours: careful.
Delvers' Guild, this is. We dig, we haul, we mind our own. And you are?
miner.heart: My mother sends a letter down every new moon. Same words each time: eat, sleep, come home. I manage two of three.
There's someone up top who waits for me at the end of every shift. That's who the lantern's really for.
I miss the smell of cut hay. Down here everything smells of stone and other people's socks.
My little brother wants to join the Guild. I want him to be a baker. We'll see who wins.
I keep a pressed flower in my helmet. From a meadow I've only seen twice.
Sometimes I'm afraid. Not of the dark. Of coming up and finding the village went on without me.
After a whole shift down, the first sunlight makes you weep. Everyone blames the brightness.
{foreman}'s gruff, but would walk into a rockfall for any of us. I know it.
I think of the Buried Seam more than I let on. Every delver does.
I've a friend up top who never writes back. I write anyway. One day they'll answer, or I'll go and knock.
miner.held.book: Reading down here? Good for you. Lantern-light makes my eyes swim past a page.
Is that {item} about the Old Delvers? Read me a bit. My letters are rusty.
The only book I've read twice is the Ore Ledger. Mostly my own line.
miner.held.bucket: Good, a bucket. Water from the walls, lava from the deep. Know which one you're scooping.
That {item} could save your life. Water on lava makes stone, and stone makes a floor.
A delver's best friend, that {item}. Keep water in it and you can climb down any cliff.
miner.held.diamond: Is that {item} real? Let me look. Oh. Oh, it is.
Put that {item} away before the whole camp sees it. Delvers go strange around diamonds.
That {item} came from deep. You didn't go into the Hush for it, did you? Tell me you didn't.
Stone gives, stone takes. With that {item}, it gave. Go home before it changes its mind.
miner.held.emerald: That {item}'s the colour of grass. I'd nearly forgotten grass.
Now we can talk business. Hold that {item} up where I can admire it.
That {item} would buy a lot of torches. A lot. Ask me how many.
miner.held.food: Is that {item}? Smells better than our stew. Don't tell anyone I said that.
Eat that {item} before the long tunnels, not halfway down them.
You wouldn't be sharing that {item}, would you? No? Fair. I wouldn't either.
miner.held.gold: That {item} catches the lantern light nicely. Soft, though. Don't make tools of it.
The Old Delvers put gold in their floors. You've got that {item} in your hand. I'd say you're ahead.
Careful with that {item}. Gold draws trouble, up top and down here.
miner.held.map: A map! Let's see. Hm. The rock never quite agrees with maps, but it's a start.
Guard that {item}. Down here a map's worth more than gold. Gold doesn't get you home.
Where's that {item} taking you? Somewhere deep, by your face.
miner.held.ore: Ore! Let me see. Mm, decent. That {item} would fill a corner of Grumble.
You've been digging. That {item}'s fresh from the wall; I can smell the stone on it.
Get that {item} to a furnace before you lose it. Ore has a way of wandering off.
miner.held.pickaxe: That {item}'s seen some rock. Keep the edge up and it'll see more.
A fellow pick-swinger! Hold that {item} loose and let the weight do the work.
Nice heft on that {item}. Just don't swing it near the props.
When did that {item} last see a grindstone? Be honest.
miner.held.potion: What's in that {item}? It's glowing. Things that glow are either ore or trouble.
A brew! There's a hermit below who makes those, they say. I've never dared try one.
Drink that {item} before you need it. You can't drink with a hisser in your face.
miner.held.sword: Expecting trouble with that {item}? Fair enough, down here.
A sword's no good in a tunnel one wide. Remember that before you swing that {item}.
Keep that {item} handy in the long tunnels. Rattlers don't wait while you change tools.
miner.held.tnt: Put that down. Gently. Then walk away from it. Then come back and explain yourself.
Is that {item}? In a camp? Under a propped roof? Have you met roofs?
We only blast far from camp, with everyone counted. Take that {item} somewhere else.
miner.held.torch: A torch! Good. Light behind you, light ahead.
Set that {item} on your right going in. Thank me on the way out.
Never enough torches. Everyone says that, and then nobody carries enough.
miner.joke: What did the hisser say to the delver? Nobody knows. Nobody ever hears the end of that conversation.
How many delvers does it take to light a lantern? Three. One to light it, two to argue whose turn it was.
I asked the rock how it was doing. Nothing. Stone-faced, as usual.
Why's the Deepwatch so serious? You'd be too, if your best friend was a wall.
What do you call a delver who digs straight down? A short story.
My pick and I have an understanding. I swing, it complains, and the wall pays.
I'm not saying the stew's thin, but I saw my reflection in it. And a pebble.
Copper's the only thing down here that ages worse than me.
A topsider asked if the dark bothers me. I said, what dark? I'd lit forty torches.
Zombies love delvers. Well. They love the taste.
You can always tell a delver's been at your table. The bread's gone and there's gravel in the butter.
I've been down so long my knees creak in the same key as the roof.
Grumble squeaks, the roof creaks, and {foreman} sighs. Together, it's nearly a song.
miner.news: Grumble jumped the rails again. Took three of us and a lot of words to set it right.
Word from the Guildhall: dues are going up. Word from me: no they're not.
A Deepwatch runner came through. Said the cave roads are quiet. They always say that.
Somebody's been eating the glow berries out of the stores. I have my suspicions. They point at {foreman}.
We broke into a cave last week and a hisser was waiting. We're all fine. The cart's a bit shorter.
The new face is thick with redstone. The whole drift glows while we work it. Like digging inside an ember.
There's talk of the Guild opening another camp nearby. Talk's cheap. Timber isn't.
Ledger day's coming. {foreman} reads out everyone's tally and pretends not to have favourites.
Water broke through in the old drift. We walled it off. Lost a good pick to it, though.
Three nights back we heard a rumble from below. Not a fall. Something else. We're not talking about it.
Fresh bread came down the shaft yesterday. Fresh-ish. It's a long shaft.
miner.night: Can't sleep. The rock's settling. It sounds like someone turning over in bed.
At night I think about the sky. All that air with nothing holding it up. Terrifying.
Only the coals for light now. I like them. They don't ask anything of you.
Some nights, far below, you can almost hear the Hush. A quiet that has a sound to it.
I dream of rain on a roof. A wooden roof. With sky on top of it.
The empty hook over the door. Every Guild camp has one. At night I look at it longer.
If you hear knocking in the walls at night, it's water. Probably. Go back to sleep.
miner.past: My first shift, I was so scared I lit nine torches in a tunnel four paces long.
My grandmother dug copper before the Guild had a hall. Said she could smell a good seam.
I'm a farmer's child. Turned out I liked digging, just not waiting for rain.
Took my Guild oath with a lantern in one hand and a pick in the other. Then dropped both.
The Guildhall's long table has every member's mark cut into it. Mine's crooked. I was nervous.
I've worked more shifts than I can count on one hand. Two hands, if I'm honest. I'm not always honest.
Before the Guild I hauled stone for a mason. Same rock, less dark, worse pay.
My first foreman told me: the rock doesn't hate you. It doesn't love you either. Remember that.
I learned to sound a roof from an old delver who was half deaf. Felt it through the haft, they said.
I was cut off behind a fall once. Three days. Sang every song I knew, twice. The diggers asked me to stop.
I first came down to pay off a debt. Stayed because I liked it. Don't tell my creditor.
As an apprentice I carried the water bucket a whole shift. Taught me where water hides.
I met {foreman} on my second shift. Got shouted at for leaning on a prop. Haven't leaned since.
My first gold, I spent on a new lantern and a very bad hat.
miner.plata: Near the surface we sometimes break into a silver husk in the stone. Empty. Shaped like a person. I don't like it.
Old Hesk tells of folk who shed their skins like silverfish. Silver folk. I laughed. Then I found a husk.
If a stranger on the road won't eat with you, won't shake your hand, and won't meet your eye, walk on. That's all.
Silverfish in the stone are bad enough. If the tales are true, some of them walk on two legs.
A traveller came down once, asking too many questions about our shaft. Left no footprints in the dust. I'm sure of it.
Smooth grey stone near the top that breaks too easy? Leave it. Something might be sleeping in it.
The silver folk? A tale for children. So why does every old delver tap a stone twice before breaking it?
miner.player.damaged: That tool's on its last legs. Get it to an anvil before it breaks mid-swing.
That thing's about to give up. Don't be deep in a tunnel when it does.
Worn tools snap at the worst time. Mend it now, {player}.
Hear that? That's your tool begging for rest. Mend it, or carry a spare.
miner.player.hungry: I can hear your stomach from here. Eat something.
Have some stew. Hungry folk swing wild.
When did you last eat? Don't answer. Just eat.
There's bread in the stores. Take some. The rock will wait.
miner.player.hurt: You're bleeding. Sit. Bread and a bandage first, then you can tell me who did it.
You look like the rock won. Rest a while, {player}.
Easy, easy. Hurt folk make mistakes down here. Sit by the fire.
Who did that to you? Rattler? Hisser? Your own pick? No judgement.
miner.player.unarmored: No helmet? Down here? The roof's not your friend, {player}.
You're dressed for a picnic. Find some armour before the long tunnels.
Bare-headed in a mine. My mother would faint. I nearly have.
The rattlers will love you. All that soft. Get some iron on.
miner.rumor: Old Hesk swore there's {rumor_name} out {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist}. Take rope.
If you're wandering, try heading {rumor_dir}. They say there's {rumor_name} that way, {rumor_dist} off.
A runner told us of {rumor_name}, {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}. Runners exaggerate, but never about distance.
Head {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist} or so, and you'll find {rumor_name}. Or it'll find you.
{foreman} won't say it, but there's {rumor_name} {rumor_dir} of here. I'd guess {rumor_dist}.
We felt a draught from the {rumor_dir} last week. Hesk would say that's {rumor_name}, breathing.
Want something to do? There's {rumor_name} out {rumor_dir}. {foreman} has it noted in the Ledger's margin.
My cousin in the Guild swore by {rumor_name}, somewhere {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist} through the rock.
They say there's {rumor_name} {rumor_dir} of {place}. No more than {rumor_dist}, by the sound of it. Bring a friend.
If you go {rumor_dir}, keep your eyes open for {rumor_name}. It's {rumor_dist} off, they reckon.
Sound carries in rock. Some nights we hear things from the {rumor_dir}. Hesk says that's {rumor_name}.
A Deepwatch runner marked {rumor_name} for us: {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist}. Didn't say much else. They never do.
Folk who come through from the {rumor_dir} talk of {rumor_name}. Never mind what else they talk of.
Strip-mining {rumor_dir}? Keep at it and you'd hit {rumor_name}. Give it {rumor_dist}.
I once followed an old rail {rumor_dir} till I lost my nerve. Hesk says it runs on to {rumor_name}.
There's {rumor_name} {rumor_dir} of here, {rumor_dist}. I've not been. I'm not brave, just honest about it.
Mind the roof if you go looking for {rumor_name}, {rumor_dir} of here. Nobody's propped that rock.
miner.rumor.none: No rumours lately. The rock's been keeping its secrets.
Nothing new. The last tale I heard was Old Hesk's, and that one had a dragon in it.
Quiet times. No runners, no tales, no trouble. I'm suspicious.
I've heard nothing worth repeating. And I repeat most things.
Nothing. Ask the Deepwatch, if you can get one of them to talk.
Not a whisper. Come back after the next runner passes through.
miner.work: Today's face is iron with a copper streak. Good honest rock.
Prop every three paces. Four if the rock's sound. Five if you're a fool.
Never rob a pillar. The ore in it is holding up the ore above you.
Deepslate wears a pick twice as fast. Keep a spare, and keep both sharp.
We cut the seam, sort the ore, cart it out, and {foreman} writes it in the Ledger. Then we do it again.
A dull pick goes to the grindstone, not back to the wall. Dull tools make careless delvers.
Gravel in the roof? Get out from under it. Gravel doesn't wait to be asked.
Sand and gravel fall. Stone stays. Learn which is which before you need to.
Water seeping from the face means a buried lake close by. Plug it, mark it, move on.
When you break into a cave, stop. Listen. Then light it. Then step in.
If the wall's warm, there's lava behind it. Don't find out how much.
Raw iron in the bins, coal in the scuttle, copper in the cart. Gold goes to {foreman} and nobody else.
I've twelve carts to fill this week. I'm at nine and a half. Grumble lost the half on a bend.
Rails get checked every morning. A cart off the rails is a cart on your foot.
Lantern at the face, lantern at the turn, lantern at the shaft. Light behind you, light ahead.
Strip-mining's honest work, but dull. I sing to the rock. It hasn't sung back. Yet.
We dig in pairs. One swings, one watches the roof. Swap often, or you both stop seeing it.
Diamonds sit deep, near the lava, in the hard grey stone. Worth the trip. Not worth dying for.
Every cart that goes up, we ring the rail once. The whole camp hears it and knows we're working.
The ladder shaft's the way up we use. Never climb it with full arms. Ask me how I know.
warden.adventure: Going down the road? Go as far as the last torch, then think hard.
If the stone turns black and soft and pulses under your feet, walk away. Slowly. Silently.
That's the Hush. Something lives there that hunts by sound. We call it the Listener. Don't let it hear you.
Diamonds lie deep, down in the deepslate. So does everything else that wants to eat you.
Take a water bucket for the lava, a pick for the walls, and twice the torches you think you'll need.
If you find a flooded hall, don't dive for treasure. Something down there is already swimming.
The purple caves that ring when you step? Geodes. Safe enough. Beautiful, too.
In the green caves with the hanging berries, the air is sweet and the pond-folk are friendly. Rest there.
Light behind you, light ahead. The Guild says it, and the Guild is right.
Mark your way with torches on one side only. Then you'll always know which way is back.
If you find anything carved with a lantern over crossed picks, that's the Old Delvers. Tread respectful.
warden.chat: The road below us runs on for miles. We only hold this stretch of it. That's enough.
Every watch, somebody writes a line in the Log. Even if the line is "nothing came".
Most days, "nothing came" is the best line in the Log.
The banner's a white lantern on black. The only lantern down here that never goes out.
Guild carts come up the road once a season with flour and arrows. We cheer them like a fair day.
You learn to sleep with one ear open. Some of us sleep with both open.
Hissers are the worst of it. You don't hear them coming. Just that hiss, and then you're praying.
Rattlers I don't mind. A skeleton comes at you honest, clattering all the way.
Spiders climb the walls and come over the top. That's why the crenels are set so close.
Cave spiders are small and nasty and they come in threes. Always carry milk for the bite.
The dripstone over the road drips all night. You stop hearing it after a month. Then you hear it in your dreams.
Never stand under a pointed dripstone. They fall, and they don't miss.
The brazier is the heart of the post. If it goes out, somebody's in trouble.
{captain} says the walls were here before any of us. The stones say they're older still.
The Watch is older than the Guild. Older than the village charters, some say.
I miss rain. You don't know you love rain until you've gone a season without it.
Bread goes hard down here in two days. We dunk it in the stew and call it a feast.
We bake in the mess oven once a week. That smell is the closest thing to home in these caves.
Don't touch the lever by the Deepgate. Not for a dare, not for a bet. Not ever.
People ask what's behind the Deepgate. A stair. The Long Stair. That's all I know, and all I want to.
The miners are good folk. Loud, though. You can hear a Guild camp a mile off.
When a delver goes missing, we're the ones who go looking. We don't always find them.
Torches every ten paces along the road. Leave a dark patch and something crawls out of it.
The archers keep score on the targets. The knights pretend not to care. They care.
Our walls aren't high. They don't need to be. Down here, nothing comes from the sky.
The Hush, we call the black places where the sculk grows. Down there, sound is all that matters.
Lava light is pretty, until you remember what it is.
If you hear water where there was no water yesterday, back away. Aquifers break through without asking.
A flooded hall is a drowned hall. Something always lives in the deep water.
I've counted every stone in the gatehouse arch. Two hundred and twelve. Long watches.
We chalk the names of the lost on the barracks wall. It's a long wall.
I write home when the Guild carts come. They carry the letters up. Half of them get there.
There's a tally by the gate of every hisser we've stopped short of the wall. It's a big tally.
{captain} went down the Long Stair once, with the Long Patrol. Twelve went. Five came back. Don't ask about it.
Years back, the Watch went to see if the hermit in the green caves was a monster. They came back fed and carrying mushrooms.
See the lantern carved over the Deepgate arch? Our banner was copied from it. The Old Delvers cut it long before us.
warden.chat.close: You know, {player}, I'd trust you on the wall beside me. I don't say that lightly.
If I fall on the road, tell my people up top that I held. Will you?
When my years on the watch are done, I'll walk up into the sun and never come down. Come and find me.
You're the only one who visits who isn't selling something or running from something.
I've told you things I haven't told the others. Keep them, will you? Below, we hold.
warden.chat.new: New to the road? Keep close to the torches and you'll do fine.
Don't mind us. We're gruff with everyone at first. It's the dark.
First time at a Deepwatch post? We don't bite. The spiders do.
You'll learn our ways. Lamp lit, road watched, gate shut. That's most of it.
warden.greet: {player}. The road's quiet. Let's keep it that way.
Lamp lit, road watched, gate shut. And now a visitor. Good.
Welcome to {place}. Wipe the cave muck off your boots.
Good {time}, {player}. Or so the watch-candle tells me.
Ah, {player}. Anything follow you up the road?
Stand easy, {player}. You're inside the walls now.
{name} of the Deepwatch, on watch. What do you need?
Mind the brazier, {player}. It bites.
Come sit a while, {player}. The stone won't miss you.
Below, we hold. And today you're below with us.
You've got that look. Long walk through dark places?
Easy, {player}. Nothing gets past this gate that we don't see first.
Ho, {player}. Bring any news down with you?
Quiet day at {place}. Too quiet, some would say. I'd say lucky.
If you're after {captain}, look by the Log. That's where {captain} lives.
Keep your torch up and your voice down, {player}, and you're welcome here.
A face that isn't one of ours. Nice change.
{player}. Good. I'd rather see you than another rattler.
Come through, come through. The road's no place to stand about.
I heard your boots a long way off. You walk loud, {player}.
Warm yourself at the fire, {player}. The deep road takes it out of you.
Hm? Oh. Sorry, I was listening to the road. What is it, {player}?
Light to you, {player}. That's how the miners say it. It's grown on us.
warden.greet.evening: Evening, {player}. The lamp watch is just starting.
Good evening. Up top the sun's going down. Down here we just light another candle.
Evening. Come for supper or come for the company?
warden.greet.friend: {player}! Who walks the road? Ha. I know who. Come in.
There's a seat by the brazier with your name on it, {player}.
Below, we hold, {player}. And it's easier holding with you about.
You're back! The others owe me a copper. I said you'd live.
{player}, my friend. Sit. Tell me what the dark's been doing.
Ah, the one who means to walk back up. And you did. Welcome.
I saved you some of the stew. Don't tell {captain}.
Good to see you whole, {player}. Truly.
{player}! Let me look at you. Still all your fingers? Good.
Back again? The road must like you.
There you are. I was starting to count you among the lost.
warden.greet.morning: Morning, {player}. Not that the stone knows it.
The watch-candle says morning. I'll take its word.
Morning. The grey watch is the coldest one. Come stand by the fire.
warden.greet.night: It's the dark watch, {player}. Speak soft, the others are sleeping.
Late to be on the road. What's chasing you?
Night, {player}. If you can't sleep, you can stand watch with me.
Quiet now. At night every sound carries up the road.
warden.greet.stranger: Halt! Who walks the road? ...You don't know the answer. Then state your business, and plainly.
Hold there. This is {place}, a post of the Deepwatch. What brings you up the road?
Stop where you are and show me your hands. Empty? Good. Now, who are you?
Halt, stranger. Nobody comes this deep for the air. What's your business?
Easy. Lower that and we'll talk. You've walked into the Deepwatch.
You came out of the rock like a mole. Not many find us that way. Name yourself.
Halt and be known. If you're honest, you've nothing to fear from us.
Hold. You may pass along the road, but you don't pass the gate behind us. Understood?
Stranger on the road! ...No, stand down, it's only a traveller. You, step into the light.
You're not Guild and you're not Watch. So what are you, this far down?
Here's how it goes, stranger: your blade stays sheathed, and ours stay sheathed. Fair?
The answer to "who walks the road" is "one who means to walk back up". Learn it. Now, your name?
warden.heart: I'd give a month's pay to see a sunrise. Just one, from the top of a hill.
Some nights I think about walking up the road and never coming back. Then the candle burns down and I check the lamp.
My people up top don't really know what I do. They think I guard a door. I suppose I do.
The quiet isn't the hard part. It's what the quiet might be hiding.
We're not heroes. We're the reason nobody needs one.
{captain} carries more than the rest of us put together. I wish I could take some of it.
When I hear a miner laughing on the road, that's my pay. That's the whole of it.
I'm afraid of the Deepgate. There, I've said it. Everyone here is, and nobody says it.
I'm not afraid of the dark anymore. I'm afraid of whatever doesn't need light.
Below, we hold. Above, they sleep. I like knowing someone up there sleeps easy because of us.
warden.held.book: Reading? The Log's the only book here, and it's grim going.
That {item} would pass a long watch. Lend it when you're done?
Stories, I hope. We've all heard each other's.
warden.held.bow: That {item} would do well on our wall. Count your arrows, though.
Rattlers will outshoot you in the open. Use the corners.
A bow down here is worth two up top. Nothing climbs as fast as an arrow flies.
warden.held.diamond: Put that {item} away before every delver from here to the camps smells it.
Diamonds. Deep ones. You've been somewhere you shouldn't, I'd wager.
Pretty. The deep gives those up rarely, and never for free.
warden.held.emerald: An emerald. Save it for the miners; they trade fair.
That {item} would buy a lot of arrows off the Guild carts.
Green stone, good coin. Don't flash it on the road.
warden.held.flower: A flower! I haven't seen one in a season. May I smell it?
That {item} doesn't belong down here. Neither do we, I suppose.
Put it by the Log. Things grow so rarely here.
warden.held.food: Is that {item}? Real food? You're welcome back any time.
Eat while you can. The road doesn't wait for full bellies.
That smells better than anything our cook has made all season.
warden.held.gold: Gold's worth less than bread down here. Still, it shines nicely by the brazier.
Mind who sees that {item}. Greed has a long arm.
The Old Delvers set gold into their stone. You'll see it in the old halls, inlaid in the black.
warden.held.map: Let me see that {item}. Hm. Our road's not on it. Most aren't.
Maps are good. Maps of the deep are guesses with lines on.
Mark the post on it. Then if you're ever lost, you'll know where the light is.
warden.held.ore: Fresh from the stone? The miners would buy that {item} off you.
Ore on the road. Watch for thieves. Not everyone down here is honest.
That {item} came out of the rock the hard way. Look after it.
warden.held.pickaxe: That {item} will see you through stone. Mind what's on the other side.
A good pick and good sense. Bring both down the road.
Tap the roof before you trust it. And with that {item}, tap it twice.
warden.held.potion: A brew? Night-sight, I hope. Good for the deep road.
Careful with unmarked bottles. I drank one once and saw colours for a day.
Keep a healing draught close down here. Ask anyone on the wall.
warden.held.shield: Good. A shield stops a rattler's arrow and a hisser's spite both.
Keep that {item} up and your head down. That's half our drill.
Wise. Most who come up the road wish they'd brought one.
warden.held.sword: Keep that {item} oiled. The damp eats steel down here.
A fair blade. Strike, step back, strike. Never chase.
Blade out inside the walls? Put it up, friend. You're safe here.
warden.held.tnt: Put that away! Not inside the walls!
That {item} near the brazier? Do you want the roof down on all of us?
Mind the roof. Mind it twice with that thing in your hands.
warden.held.torch: Light behind you, light ahead. Plant those as you go.
That {item} is worth more than gold in the deep.
Hold it high. A torch held low only lights your boots.
warden.joke: How many wardens does it take to light a torch? One to light it, three to say it's crooked.
A hisser walks up to the gate. I call, "Who walks the road?" It says, "Ssss." Worst answer we've had all year.
Why don't rattlers ever stand watch? No guts. I've told that one forty times. It still works.
The stew tonight is "mystery stew". The mystery is whether it was ever food.
Our archers can hit a spider at forty paces. Our cook can't hit the pot at two.
There's a slime down the road that comes up every few weeks. Same slime every time. We call it Old Wobble.
A zombie came up the road once in a delver's helmet. Best-dressed thing we'd seen all season.
What's the difference between a cave spider and a warden on the dark watch? The spider's awake.
Someone asked if it gets lonely down here. I said no, the bats visit. Constantly. They never leave.
I bet a miner my boots the roof wouldn't drip on me all night. Walked home barefoot.
warden.news: A Guild cart came up the road last week. Flour, arrows, two letters and one very angry chicken.
The aquifer under the side drift is weeping again. We've scratched a mark on the wall to watch it rise.
Torches went out along the far bend two nights back. Not burned out. Knocked down.
The miners say the ore's running rich this season. More of them on the road means more of us on the wall.
One of the archers put an arrow through a rattler's bow at fifty paces yesterday. We're still not over it.
{captain} has been at the Log late every night this week. Nobody's asked why.
A hisser got as far as the second torch before we stopped it. The second torch. That's close.
We heard the Deepgate settle on its hinges last night. Just the stone moving. Probably.
The cook found a cave spider nest under the mess flagstones. We ate cold for two days while we burned it out.
Bats have been thick on the road this month. Means warm weather up top, the miners say.
A lost delver wandered in yesterday after three days in the dark. Ate everything we had. Kissed the brazier.
warden.night: Night on the wall is the long watch. You count torches. You count breaths.
At night the road gets busy. Things smell the brazier's warmth from a long way off.
The dark watch is when the Deepgate is loudest. Hinges, settling. That's all. I tell myself that's all.
Keep your voice low once the candle passes midnight. Sound carries up the road, and down it.
{captain} walks the wall at night when sleep won't come. Which is most nights.
Night is when the drowned come up from the flooded halls, dripping. You smell them before you see them.
Funny, isn't it? It's always dark down here, but you still feel the night come on.
warden.past: I joined the Watch at sixteen. Thought it'd be glory. It's mostly cold feet and counting.
My village had a mine. One shift, my father went down and didn't come up. So I came down to keep others coming up.
I trained at another post, further along the road. We lost it to a flood. The water just came.
Before the Watch I was a baker's apprentice. I still knead the bread here, when there's flour.
My first night on the wall, a hisser got close enough that I could hear it breathe. I didn't sleep for a week.
The oath is short. "I keep the lamp. I hold the road. I do not go down." I've never broken a word of it.
When I came, there were nine of us here. Now it's five. Most went home. Not all.
{captain} took me in when no other post would. I'd been sent off for sleeping on watch. Never again.
The year the aquifer broke, we fought drowned in the road for three days. The water was up to our knees.
I grew up topside, in a village by a river. Down here I dream about fish.
My first patrol, we found a lost delver sitting in the dark with no torch, humming. Took three days to get a word out.
We held this gate for a whole night once, against everything the deep road could send. The braziers never went out.
warden.plata: Delvers near the surface break stone and find silver husks inside. Empty, like a shed skin. We log every one.
The silver folk, the miners call them. Folk who shed their skins like silverfish. I thought it was a tale.
A stranger came down the road once, polite, asking too much about the gate. When we looked again, gone.
If someone on the road won't lower their hood by the brazier, keep your hand near your weapon.
The oath says "I hold the road." Against the silver folk too, if they're real. I hope they're not.
A silverfish crawled out of the wall stone last spring. The old hands pulled the whole block and burned it. Didn't say why.
warden.player.diamond: Diamond armour! You'd shame half the Watch, dressed like that.
That's a fortune on your back. Wear it well, and don't go swimming in it.
In plate like that, you could hold the gate on your own.
warden.player.hungry: You look starved. There's stew in the pot. Don't ask what's in it.
When did you last eat? Here, bread. It's hard, but it's bread.
Hunger on the road makes you careless. Eat first, explore after.
warden.player.hurt: You're bleeding. Sit. I've bandages and a heel of bread.
What did that to you? Spiders? Sit down before you fall down.
Easy, easy. You're inside the walls. Breathe.
warden.player.leather: Leather's better than nothing. Not much better, this deep.
Good leather. Now find some iron to put over it.
Leather won't stop a rattler, but it might turn a cave spider's bite. Sometimes.
warden.player.unarmored: No armour? On this road? Are you brave, or just in a hurry?
You want something between you and a rattler's arrow. Even leather.
Coming down here in your shirt. The spiders will be glad of you.
warden.rumor: The last patrol came back past {rumor_name} to the {rumor_dir}. They didn't stay long.
There's {rumor_name} {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}. It's in the Log, if you'd like to see.
The miners talk of {rumor_name} out to the {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist} or so. I've not seen it myself.
Head {rumor_dir}, {rumor_dist} or thereabouts, and you'll come on {rumor_name}. Take light.
We marked {rumor_name} on the road-map, out to the {rumor_dir}. Only a few of us have been.
If you're bent on wandering, there's {rumor_name} to the {rumor_dir}. Better that than the Hush.
I followed a lost delver's tracks once to {rumor_name}, {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}. Found them, too. Barely.
Somewhere to the {rumor_dir} lies {rumor_name}. The road doesn't go there. You'd have to dig.
An old Log entry speaks of {rumor_name}, {rumor_dist} off to the {rumor_dir}. The hand that wrote it was shaking.
A Guild cart-driver swore there was {rumor_name} to the {rumor_dir}. Cart-drivers swear a lot, but they rarely lie.
Our patrol map has {rumor_name} {rumor_dist} to the {rumor_dir}, with a little lantern drawn beside it.
Listen at the wall on a quiet watch and you'll hear something off to the {rumor_dir}. The Log says it's {rumor_name}.
{captain} once led a sweep out to {rumor_name}, to the {rumor_dir}, and came back with a sack nobody was allowed to open.
If you go {rumor_dir}, you'll find {rumor_name} {rumor_dist} along. Say the Watch sends greetings, if there's anyone to hear it.
warden.rumor.none: Nothing in the Log for a long way round. Just stone, and more stone.
No other places I know of near here. The road's all we've got.
The patrols have found nothing worth the walk, not near here. Sorry.
Not a thing. If you find something, come and tell us, and we'll write it down.
warden.work: Four watches a day by the candle. Two on the wall, one at the gate, one asleep. We turn it round.
Every watch starts the same: check the lamp, walk the road, try the Deepgate bar. Lamp lit, road watched, gate shut.
Drills at every change of watch. Step, strike, step back. Again until it's dull. Dull keeps you alive.
I walk the road out to the last torch and back. If a torch is out, I find out why.
Hissers we take at range. Archers first, and nobody goes near until it's quiet.
Rule of the gate: nobody passes the Deepgate without the captain's word. Not you, not me, not a lord with a letter.
We sweep the fallen dripstone off the road every morning. A pointed stone underfoot will lame a warden.
We don't chase anything into the dark. We hold the light and let it come to us.
A delver comes up the road hurt, we patch them up. A delver comes up the road scared, we listen.
Webs across the road get burned the moment we see them. Spiders are patient builders.
Arrows get counted every watch. An archer who loses arrows buys the next round.
Anything that comes up the road gets met here, before it reaches the miners' camps. That's the whole job.
I log every sound I can't name. Most turn out to be gravel. Some don't.
A bucket of water by every brazier, a bucket of milk by every bed. Fire and poison, the two quick deaths.
The training dummies take a beating every day and never once complain. Best recruits we have.
If something knocks on the Deepgate from the other side, the rule is simple. Log it. Don't answer.
Fresh torches go up along the road every third day, whether the old ones need it or not.
Change of watch, we say it face to face: "Below, we hold." "Above, they sleep." Then the old watch can rest.
Each season one of us runs word to the Guild camps. "Cave roads quiet." The miners laugh. They're glad of it all the same.
